predictive_services_discussion: 8/4/2026 Cooler-than-average temperatures are expected for the northern and central Plains, northern Rockies, and western Great Lakes, while remaining slightly below normal east of the Mississippi River. Extreme heat will persist throughout inland California, the central/southern Great Basin, and the Southwest into the southern Plains, with highs reaching 100°F or above. Temperatures will be near or slightly above normal for the Inland Northwest. Hot, dry, and unstable conditions will expand over western portions of the Northwest. A strengthening thermal trough creates high-risk fire potential for southwest Oregon, extending north along the Cascades to the Columbia River Gorge. Lingering breeziness amidst a very hot, dry, and unstable air mass creates similar high- risk fire conditions for the northern and eastern Great Basin. Minimum RH of 3-15% across California, the Inland Northwest, the Great Basin, and the Four Corners, and 10-20% in northern Idaho and Montana. Isolated mixed wet/dry thunderstorms from the Rockies into the northern Plains. A stronger signal for wet thunderstorms exists in southeast Arizona and southwest New Mexico, though the rest of the Southwest will see below average coverage. Showers and thunderstorms will also favor the Carolinas, Georgia, and Florida.
